topics.label: Introduction and lecture learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the introductory framing, course overview, and core learning objectives for the lecture on cancer causation.

topics.label: Fundamental concepts and epidemiological patterns of cancer causation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the interplay between intrinsic genetic errors, environmental exposures, and global epidemiological patterns in the development of cancer.

topics.label: Infectious agents and viral oncogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how biological pathogens promote cancer development, focusing specifically on oncogenic mechanisms and the etiology of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Mechanisms of chemical carcinogenesis and tumor promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how physical agents, chemical mutagens, metabolic activation, and tumor promoters induce cellular transformation and DNA damage across different tissue contexts.

topics.label: Methodologies and considerations for determining carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the genomic, epidemiological, and experimental methodologies used to identify carcinogens and evaluate their real-world risks.

topics.label: Lecture summary and conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the final concluding remarks and high-level summary of the lecture.
